<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<title>Data and SQL: Interview Prep</title>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible+Next:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,700;1,400&family=Bricolage+Grotesque:opsz,wght@12..96,500..800&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500;600&family=Caveat:wght@600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
  /* study-theme v4 "whiteboard": the one stylesheet every guide uses. Edit here, then run
     `npm run study:upgrade` to apply it to every guide (lib.upgrade swaps each guide's <style> for this file).
     Token names are also used inside the SVG diagrams (dg*.mjs), so rename none of them. */
  :root{
    /* light: a whiteboard. Navy ink, blue marker for actions, green for done, yellow highlighter. */
    --bg:#F5F7FA;
    --panel:#FFFFFF;
    --panel-2:#EEF2F7;
    --border:#D3DAE5;
    --text:#14213D;
    --muted:#4F5D78;
    --accent:#1B55C5;
    --accent-ink:#FFFFFF;
    --accent-soft:#E4EDFC;
    --gold:#7A5200;
    --gold-soft:#FFF1B8;
    --ok:#126B4B;
    --ok-soft:#DDF3E9;
    --code-bg:#EEF2F7;
    --danger:#B42318;
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(20,33,61,.06), 0 4px 14px rgba(20,33,61,.04);
    --mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
    --sans: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
    --display: 'Bricolage Grotesque', var(--sans);
    --hand: 'Caveat', 'Segoe Print', 'Bradley Hand', 'Comic Sans MS', cursive;
    --measure: 76ch;
  }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){
    :root:not([data-theme="light"]){
      /* dark: a chalkboard. Chalk white text, chalk blue / yellow / green accents. */
      --bg:#101A19;
      --panel:#17231F;
      --panel-2:#1E2D29;
      --border:#33493F;
      --text:#ECF1EE;
      --muted:#A9B8B1;
      --accent:#93BCFF;
      --accent-ink:#0A1730;
      --accent-soft:#1D3048;
      --gold:#F0CF6B;
      --gold-soft:#3A3216;
      --ok:#7FD6A8;
      --ok-soft:#173327;
      --code-bg:#0C1513;
      --danger:#F5A99C;
      --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4);
    }
  }
  :root[data-theme="dark"]{
    --bg:#101A19;
    --panel:#17231F;
    --panel-2:#1E2D29;
    --border:#33493F;
    --text:#ECF1EE;
    --muted:#A9B8B1;
    --accent:#93BCFF;
    --accent-ink:#0A1730;
    --accent-soft:#1D3048;
    --gold:#F0CF6B;
    --gold-soft:#3A3216;
    --ok:#7FD6A8;
    --ok-soft:#173327;
    --code-bg:#0C1513;
    --danger:#F5A99C;
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4);
  }

  *{box-sizing:border-box;}
  html,body{margin:0;padding:0;}
  html{color-scheme:light dark; scroll-padding-top:16px;}
  body{
    background:var(--bg);
    color:var(--text);
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:16px;
    line-height:1.6;
    -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
    text-rendering:optimizeLegibility;
  }
  a{color:var(--accent); text-underline-offset:2px;}
  :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:2px; border-radius:4px;}
  ::selection{background:var(--gold-soft); color:var(--text);}

  .app{display:flex; min-height:100vh;}

  /* ---------- Sidebar ---------- */
  .sidebar{
    width:288px;
    flex:0 0 288px;
    border-right:1px solid var(--border);
    background:var(--panel);
    padding:18px 14px 24px;
    position:sticky;
    top:0;
    height:100vh;
    overflow-y:auto;
    scrollbar-width:thin;
  }
  .side-top{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:8px; margin:0 0 14px;}
  .home-link{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; color:var(--muted); text-decoration:none; padding:6px 8px; border-radius:8px;}
  .home-link:hover{color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft);}
  .theme-btn{font:inherit; font-size:15px; line-height:1; width:34px; height:34px; color:var(--muted); background:transparent; border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px; cursor:pointer;}
  .theme-btn:hover{color:var(--accent); border-color:var(--accent);}
  .brand{
    font-size:13.5px;
    line-height:1.45;
    color:var(--muted);
    padding:0 8px 16px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
    margin-bottom:14px;
  }
  .brand b{display:block; font-family:var(--display); font-size:19px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:-0.01em; color:var(--text);}
  .brand br{display:none;}
  .nav-item{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    justify-content:space-between;
    gap:10px;
    width:100%;
    text-align:left;
    padding:9px 10px;
    border-radius:9px;
    border:1px solid transparent;
    background:transparent;
    color:var(--text);
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:15px;
    line-height:1.35;
    cursor:pointer;
    margin-bottom:2px;
  }
  .nav-item:hover{background:var(--panel-2);}
  .nav-item.active{background:var(--accent-soft); color:var(--text); font-weight:700; box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--accent);}
  .nav-num{font-size:12.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--muted); width:20px; flex:0 0 20px;}
  .nav-item.active .nav-num{color:var(--accent);}
  .nav-label{flex:1;}
  .nav-count{
    font-size:12px;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;
    color:var(--muted);
    background:var(--panel-2);
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:1px 7px;
    border-radius:999px;
  }
  .nav-item.complete .nav-count{color:var(--ok); border-color:var(--ok); background:var(--ok-soft);}
  .progress-box{
    margin-top:20px;
    padding:14px 12px;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:12px;
    background:var(--panel-2);
  }
  .progress-box .label{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:700; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:8px; text-transform:lowercase;}
  .progress-box .label::first-letter{text-transform:uppercase;}
  .progress-track{height:8px; border-radius:999px; background:var(--border); overflow:hidden;}
  .progress-fill{height:100%; background:var(--ok); width:0%; transition:width .25s ease;}
  .progress-num{margin-top:8px; font-size:13.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--text);}
  .reset-btn{
    margin-top:10px;
    width:100%;
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:13px;
    color:var(--muted);
    background:transparent;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:8px;
    padding:7px 8px;
    cursor:pointer;
  }
  .reset-btn:hover{color:var(--danger);border-color:var(--danger);}

  /* ---------- Main ---------- */
  .main{
    flex:1;
    min-width:0;
    padding:40px 48px 96px;
    max-width:1080px;
  }
  .hero{margin-bottom:36px;}
  .hero .eyebrow-free{display:none;}
  .hero h1{
    font-family:var(--display);
    font-size:clamp(28px, 3.4vw, 40px);
    line-height:1.12;
    margin:0 0 14px;
    font-weight:700;
    letter-spacing:-0.02em;
    text-wrap:balance;
  }
  .hero p{color:var(--muted); max-width:68ch; margin:0 0 6px; font-size:16.5px;}
  .hero p strong{color:var(--text);}
  .hero .source-note{font-size:13.5px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:18px; line-height:1.9;}

  .section-head{
    display:flex;
    align-items:baseline;
    gap:12px;
    margin:44px 0 14px;
    padding-bottom:12px;
    border-bottom:2px solid var(--text);
  }
  .section-head .num{font-family:var(--display); color:var(--accent); font-size:17px; font-weight:700; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}
  .section-head h2{font-family:var(--display); font-size:26px; line-height:1.2; margin:0; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:-0.015em;}
  .section-head .count{margin-left:auto; font-size:13.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--muted); white-space:nowrap;}

  .qcard{
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:14px;
    background:var(--panel);
    margin-bottom:10px;
    overflow:hidden;
    box-shadow:var(--shadow);
  }
  .qcard:hover{border-color:var(--accent);}
  .qcard.open{border-color:var(--accent); box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent), var(--shadow);}
  .qcard.focused{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .qhead{
    display:flex;
    align-items:flex-start;
    gap:14px;
    padding:15px 18px;
    cursor:pointer;
    user-select:none;
  }
  .qcheck{
    margin-top:3px;
    flex:0 0 auto;
    width:20px;height:20px;
    border-radius:6px;
    border:1.5px solid var(--muted);
    display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;
    cursor:pointer;
    background:var(--panel);
  }
  .qcheck:hover{border-color:var(--ok);}
  .qcheck.done{background:var(--ok); border-color:var(--ok);}
  .qcheck.done::after{content:"✓"; color:var(--panel); font-size:13px; font-weight:700;}
  .qmain{flex:1; min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px;}
  .qtext{flex:1; font-size:16.5px; line-height:1.4; font-weight:700;}
  .qtext.done-text{color:var(--muted); font-weight:500;}
  .qchips{display:flex; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .qsec,.qcore{font-size:12px; padding:1px 8px; border-radius:99px; border:1px solid var(--border); color:var(--muted); background:var(--panel-2);}
  .qcore{color:var(--gold); border-color:var(--gold); background:var(--gold-soft);}
  .qsum{font-size:14.5px; color:var(--muted); line-height:1.5; max-width:var(--measure);}
  .qcard.open .qsum{display:none;}
  .qchevron{
    flex:0 0 auto;
    color:var(--muted);
    font-size:20px;
    line-height:1;
    transform:rotate(0deg);
    transition:transform .15s ease;
    margin-top:2px;
  }
  .qcard.open .qchevron{transform:rotate(90deg); color:var(--accent);}
  .qbody{
    display:none;
    padding:2px 22px 22px 52px;
    border-top:1px solid var(--border);
    font-size:16px;
    line-height:1.65;
  }
  .qcard.open .qbody{display:block; padding-top:18px;}
  /* Prose keeps a readable line length; tables, code and diagrams may use the full card width. */
  .qbody > p, .qbody > ul, .qbody > ol, .qbody > blockquote, .qbody > .callout, .qbody > h3, .qbody > h4{max-width:var(--measure);}
  .qbody p{margin:0 0 14px;}
  .qbody ul, .qbody ol{margin:0 0 14px; padding-left:22px;}
  .qbody li{margin-bottom:7px;}
  .qbody li::marker{color:var(--accent);}
  .qbody strong{color:var(--text); font-weight:700;}
  .qbody h3, .qbody h4{font-family:var(--display); font-size:17px; margin:20px 0 8px; letter-spacing:-0.01em;}
  code{
    font-family:var(--mono);
    background:var(--code-bg);
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:0 5px;
    border-radius:5px;
    font-size:0.875em;
    overflow-wrap:anywhere;
  }
  pre{
    font-family:var(--mono);
    background:var(--code-bg);
    color:var(--text);
    padding:14px 16px;
    border-radius:10px;
    overflow-x:auto;
    font-size:13.5px;
    line-height:1.65;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    tab-size:2;
  }
  pre code{background:none; border:0; padding:0; font-size:inherit;}
  /* syntax colouring added by the engine (comments, strings, keywords, numbers) */
  .tk-c{color:var(--muted); font-style:italic;}
  .tk-s{color:var(--ok);}
  .tk-k{color:var(--accent); font-weight:500;}
  .tk-n{color:var(--gold);}
  /* A diagram is a whiteboard (a chalkboard in dark mode): engine.js redraws the tidy SVG by hand
     (see "sketch" there) and this sets the board, the marker strokes and the handwriting. */
  .diagram{
    background:var(--panel);
    border:1.5px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:14px;
    box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 4px var(--panel), inset 0 0 0 5px var(--panel-2);
    padding:16px;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    overflow-x:auto;
  }
  .diagram svg{display:block; margin:0 auto; max-width:100%; height:auto;}
  /* Handwriting is sized by x-height (font-size-adjust) so it reads as large as the type it replaces.
     These values are the largest at which every label in every guide still fits its box:
     `node scripts/study/audit-diagrams.mjs` proves it, so re-run that after changing them. */
  .diagram svg.sk text:not(.sk-code){font-family:var(--hand); font-size-adjust:.50; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.012em;}
  .diagram svg.sk text[font-family="var(--mono)"]:not(.sk-code){font-size-adjust:.60;}
  .diagram svg.sk text.sk-caps:not(.sk-code){font-size-adjust:.44;}
  .diagram svg.sk text[font-weight="600"]:not(.sk-code), .diagram svg.sk text[font-weight="700"]:not(.sk-code){font-weight:700;}
  /* Code and SQL are never handwritten (engine.js sketchIsCode): .sk-code keeps the authored type. */
  .diagram svg.sk .sk-s{stroke-width:1.9px; stroke-linecap:round; stroke-linejoin:round;}
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference){
    .diagram svg.sk .sk-d{animation:sk-draw .5s ease-out backwards; animation-delay:var(--d, 0ms);}
    .diagram svg.sk .sk-t{animation:sk-ink .35s ease-out backwards; animation-delay:var(--d, 0ms);}
  }
  @keyframes sk-draw{ from{stroke-dasharray:1; stroke-dashoffset:1; fill-opacity:0;} to{stroke-dasharray:1; stroke-dashoffset:0;} }
  @keyframes sk-ink{ from{opacity:0;} }
  /* The tidy original stays one click away (the switch under each diagram), drawn exactly as authored. */
  .diagram.tidy{background:var(--panel-2); border-width:1px; border-radius:12px; box-shadow:none;}
  .dg-bar{display:flex; justify-content:flex-end; gap:4px; margin:10px 0 -4px; position:sticky; left:0;}
  .dg-bar button{
    font:500 11.5px/1 var(--sans); color:var(--muted); background:transparent; cursor:pointer;
    border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:999px; padding:5px 9px;
  }
  .dg-bar button:hover{color:var(--text); border-color:var(--border);}
  .dg-bar button[aria-pressed="true"]{color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft); border-color:transparent;}
  .dg-bar button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .dg-bar button[data-dg="zoom"]{margin-left:6px; border-color:var(--border);}
  /* On a phone a 900-unit drawing squeezed into 300px is unreadable, so it keeps a readable size
     and scrolls sideways inside its board instead. */
  @media (max-width:760px){ .diagram svg{min-width:680px;} }
  /* Enlarged view (engine.js enlargeDiagram) */
  .dg-zoom{
    width:min(1500px, calc(100vw - 24px)); max-width:none; max-height:calc(100vh - 24px); padding:0;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:16px; background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); overflow:hidden;
  }
  .dg-zoom[open]{display:flex; flex-direction:column;}
  .dg-zoom::backdrop{background:rgba(10,16,30,.6);}
  .dg-zoom-top{
    display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; padding:8px 10px 8px 16px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border); font:500 12.5px/1.3 var(--sans); color:var(--muted);
  }
  .dg-zoom-close{
    font:600 13px/1 var(--sans); color:var(--text); background:var(--panel); cursor:pointer;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:999px; padding:9px 14px;
  }
  .dg-zoom-close:hover{border-color:var(--accent); color:var(--accent);}
  .dg-zoom-close:focus-visible, .dg-zoom-body:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:-2px;}
  .dg-zoom-body{overflow:auto; padding:14px;}
  .dg-zoom .diagram{margin:0;}
  .dg-zoom .diagram svg{width:100%; min-width:860px; max-width:none;}
  .dg-zoom .dg-bar [data-dg="zoom"]{display:none;}
  .diagram.lightbg{background:#F8FAFC; border-color:#CBD5E1;}
  .diagram.lightbg .codelabel{color:#334155;}
  .tag{
    display:inline-block;
    font-size:12px;
    color:var(--gold);
    background:var(--gold-soft);
    border:1px solid var(--gold);
    border-radius:6px;
    padding:1px 7px;
    margin-bottom:10px;
  }
  .tscroll{overflow-x:auto; margin:0 0 16px;}
  .tscroll > table.cmp{margin:0;}
  table.cmp{
    width:100%;
    border-collapse:collapse;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    font-size:14.5px;
    line-height:1.5;
  }
  table.cmp th, table.cmp td{
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:9px 12px;
    text-align:left;
    vertical-align:top;
  }
  table.cmp th{background:var(--panel-2); font-size:13.5px; font-weight:700;}
  table.cmp tr:nth-child(odd) td{background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--panel-2) 45%, transparent);}

  .tbadge{display:inline-block; font-size:12px; font-weight:700; color:var(--gold); background:var(--gold-soft); border:1px solid var(--gold); border-radius:99px; padding:2px 10px; margin-bottom:10px;}
  .deeper{margin-top:16px; padding-top:12px; border-top:1px dashed var(--border); font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.9;}
  .deeper + .deeper{margin-top:2px; padding-top:0; border-top:0;}
  a.go{color:var(--accent); text-decoration:none; border-bottom:1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, transparent);}
  a.go:hover{border-bottom-color:var(--accent);}

  .search{width:100%; box-sizing:border-box; margin:0 0 14px; padding:10px 12px; font:inherit; font-size:14.5px; color:var(--text); background:var(--bg); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:10px;}
  .search::placeholder{color:var(--muted);}
  .search:focus{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .qcheck:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:2px;}
  mark{background:var(--gold-soft); color:var(--text); border-radius:3px; padding:0 2px;}
  .toolbar{display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center; gap:10px 16px; margin:0 0 18px; font-size:14px; color:var(--muted);}
  .toolbar .tmeta{font-size:13.5px; margin-right:auto;}
  .toolbar .tgroup{display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .toolbar button{font:inherit; font-size:13.5px; color:var(--text); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px; padding:6px 12px; cursor:pointer;}
  .toolbar button:hover{border-color:var(--accent); color:var(--accent);}
  .toolbar label{display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; cursor:pointer; white-space:nowrap;}
  .toolbar input{accent-color:var(--accent); width:15px; height:15px;}
  .empty{color:var(--muted); font-size:15px; padding:18px; border:1px dashed var(--border); border-radius:12px;}
  .pager{display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; margin-top:28px;}
  .pager button{font:inherit; font-size:14.5px; font-weight:500; color:var(--accent); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:10px; padding:12px 16px; cursor:pointer; max-width:48%; text-align:left;}
  .pager button:last-child{text-align:right;}
  .pager button:hover{border-color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft);}
  .back-btn{position:fixed; right:22px; bottom:22px; z-index:10; font:inherit; font-size:14px; font-weight:700; color:var(--accent-ink); background:var(--accent); border:0; border-radius:99px; padding:11px 18px; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.22);}
  .keys{display:inline-block; margin-top:6px;}
  kbd{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11.5px; padding:0 5px; border:1px solid var(--border); border-bottom-width:2px; border-radius:5px; background:var(--panel); color:var(--text);}
  .hero-actions{margin-top:18px; display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:10px;}
  .fc-start,.toolbar .flash-btn{font:inherit; font-weight:700; color:var(--accent-ink); background:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent); border-radius:10px; cursor:pointer;}
  .fc-start{font-size:15px; padding:10px 18px;}
  .toolbar .flash-btn{color:var(--accent-ink);}
  .toolbar .flash-btn:hover{color:var(--accent-ink);}
  .fc-start:hover,.toolbar .flash-btn:hover{filter:brightness(1.1);}
  button.fc-start.alt{background:var(--panel); color:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent);}
  button.fc-start.alt:hover{background:var(--accent-soft); filter:none;}
  a.fc-start.alt{display:inline-block; text-decoration:none; background:var(--panel); color:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent);}

  /* ---------- Flashcards ---------- */
  body.fc-lock{overflow:hidden;}
  .fc{position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:50; background:rgba(8,14,26,.6); display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:24px;}
  .fc[hidden]{display:none;}
  .fc-dialog{width:min(920px,100%); max-height:100%; display:flex; flex-direction:column; background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:18px; box-shadow:0 24px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.4); outline:none;}
  .fc-head{display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:flex-start; gap:12px; padding:18px 22px 12px;}

      q:"What do primary keys, foreign keys and constraints guarantee, and why let the database enforce them?",
      a:`<p>A <strong>constraint</strong> is a rule the database checks on every write, from every application, script and person that connects. The application can check too, but only the database cannot be bypassed.</p><table class="cmp"><tr><th>Constraint</th><th>Guarantees</th><th>Violation in the lab</th></tr><tr><td><code>PRIMARY KEY</code></td><td>Each row is unique and not null; gives a stable identity</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>FOREIGN KEY</code></td><td>A reference points at a row that exists, and a referenced row cannot vanish</td><td><code>Key (department_id)=(99) is not present in table "departments".</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>UNIQUE</code></td><td>No two rows share the value</td><td><code>Key (email)=(user1@example.com) already exists.</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>CHECK</code></td><td>A rule about the row, such as <code>balance_cents >= 0</code></td><td><code>Failing row contains (1, Ada, -5).</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>NOT NULL</code></td><td>A value must be present</td><td><code>null value in column "name" of relation "departments" violates not-null constraint</code></td></tr></table><p class="codelabel">Two real errors</p><pre class="plain">insert into employees (name, department_id, salary, hired_on) values ('Zed', 99, 1, '2020-01-01');
ERROR: insert or update on table "employees" violates foreign key constraint "employees_department_id_fkey"
DETAIL: Key (department_id)=(99) is not present in table "departments".

delete from departments where id = 1;
ERROR: update or delete on table "departments" violates foreign key constraint "employees_department_id_fkey" on table "employees"
DETAIL: Key (id)=(1) is still referenced from table "employees".</pre><ul><li><strong>Why enforce in the database:</strong> two services, a migration script and a late-night fix by hand will all write to the same tables. Application-only checks drift apart.</li><li><strong>Cost:</strong> a check on every write, and a foreign key needs an index on the referencing column or deletes from the parent get slow.</li><li>Application validation still matters for friendly error messages. The constraint is the backstop.</li></ul><p class="verified">Every output in this guide was captured on 15 Nov 2026 from PostgreSQL 17.6 in Docker, on a seeded database with 200,000 orders. Plans are trimmed and the timings vary from run to run, so read the plan shape and the row counts, not the milliseconds. Other databases and versions differ, and where it matters the card says so.</p>`

    {
      q:"What is normalisation, and when do you denormalise on purpose?",
      a:`<p><strong>Normalising</strong> means storing each fact once, so that changing it is one update and cannot leave two copies disagreeing.</p><table class="cmp"><tr><th>Form</th><th>Rule</th><th>A violation</th></tr><tr><td><strong>1NF</strong></td><td>One value per column, no repeating groups</td><td>A <code>phones</code> column holding <code>"555-1, 555-2"</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>2NF</strong></td><td>Every column depends on the whole key</td><td>In <code>order_items(order_id, product_id, product_name)</code>, the name depends on <code>product_id</code> only</td></tr><tr><td><strong>3NF</strong></td><td>Columns depend on the key, not on each other</td><td><code>employees</code> holding both <code>department_id</code> and <code>department_name</code></td></tr></table><p><strong>Denormalise on purpose</strong> when you have measured a read that is too slow and a join cannot fix it:</p><ul><li>A stored <code>order_total</code> copied from the line items, so a list page does not sum them.</li><li>A counter such as <code>comment_count</code>, updated in the same transaction.</li><li>A read model or cache built for one screen.</li></ul><p><strong>Trap:</strong> Every copy is a promise to keep it in sync. Say who updates it, in which transaction, and what repairs it when it drifts.</p><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/system-design" target="_top">System Design: data modelling</a></p>`

      q:"Why does a comparison with NULL not behave like true or false?",
      a:`<p><code>NULL</code> means <strong>unknown</strong>, not “empty”. Comparing anything with an unknown gives unknown, which <code>WHERE</code> treats as not true. SQL therefore has <strong>three-valued logic</strong>: true, false and unknown.</p><p class="codelabel">NULL = NULL is not true</p><pre>select null = null as eq,

       null is distinct from null as distinct_from,

NULL | true    | false         | true
(1 row)</pre><p class="codelabel">The row that disappears</p><pre>select name from employees where department_id <> 1;            -- 5 rows, Nora missing

      q:"WHERE or HAVING: which filter goes where?",
      a:`<p><code>WHERE</code> filters <strong>rows before</strong> they are grouped. <code>HAVING</code> filters <strong>groups after</strong> they are aggregated. A condition on a plain column belongs in <code>WHERE</code>, because it discards rows early and lets an index help.</p><p class="codelabel">Two different questions</p><pre>-- WHERE: only well-paid rows are counted
select department_id, count(*) as n from employees
where salary > 80000 group by department_id order by department_id;

-- HAVING: departments that have more than 2 people, whatever they earn
select department_id, count(*) as n from employees
group by department_id having count(*) > 2 order by department_id;</pre><p class="codelabel">Result of the first query</p><pre class="plain">department_id | n
--------------+--
            1 | 5
            2 | 3
(2 rows)</pre><p class="codelabel">Result of the second query</p><pre class="plain">department_id | n

(2 rows)</pre><ul><li>Department 1 has 5 people earning over 80,000 but 6 people in total: Fiona earns 60,000.       a:`<p>A <strong>covering index</strong> holds every column a query needs, so PostgreSQL answers from the index without touching the table (an <strong>index-only scan</strong>). A <strong>partial index</strong> indexes only the rows that match a condition, so it is small and cheap.</p><p class="codelabel">Covering with INCLUDE</p><pre>create index orders_cust_cover_idx on orders (customer_id) include (total_cents);
vacuum analyze orders;
explain (analyze, buffers) select customer_id, total_cents from orders where customer_id = 42;</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan (trimmed)</p><pre class="plain">Index Only Scan using orders_cust_cover_idx on orders  (actual rows=102 loops=1)

  Heap Blocks: exact=102
  ->  Bitmap Index Scan on orders_cust_cover_idx ...</pre><p class="codelabel">Partial index</p><pre>create index orders_refunded_idx on orders (created_at) where status = 'refunded';

where status = 'refunded' and created_at > '2025-02-01';</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan (trimmed)</p><pre class="plain">Index Scan using orders_refunded_idx on orders  (cost=0.28..12.41 rows=179 width=8) (actual rows=189 loops=1)

On a table with heavy writes, <code>Heap Fetches</code> rises and the benefit shrinks.</li><li>Partial indexes also enforce rules such as “one active subscription per user”: <code>create unique index ... where status = 'active'</code>.</li></ul>`

      q:"Why is my query not using the index?",
      a:`<p>Look at the plan before guessing. These are the usual reasons, and the first three were run in the lab.</p><table class="cmp"><tr><th>Reason</th><th>Fix</th></tr><tr><td>A <strong>function on the column</strong>: <code>lower(email) = ...</code></td><td>Index the expression, or store the value normalised</td></tr><tr><td>A <strong>type mismatch</strong>: <code>customer_id = 42.0</code></td><td>Compare like with like: <code>customer_id = 42</code></td></tr><tr><td>A <strong>leading wildcard</strong>: <code>like '%42@example.com'</code></td><td>Use a trigram (GIN) index, or search differently</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Low selectivity</strong>: most rows match</td><td>The planner is right: a full scan is cheaper</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Stale statistics</strong></td><td><code>ANALYZE</code>, and check autovacuum</td></tr></table><p class="codelabel">A function on the column</p><pre>explain (analyze) select id from customers where lower(email) = 'user42@example.com';</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan (trimmed)</p><pre class="plain">Seq Scan on customers  (cost=0.00..47.00 rows=10 width=4) (actual rows=1 loops=1)
  Filter: (lower(email) = 'user42@example.com'::text)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 1999</pre><p class="codelabel">After indexing the expression</p><pre>create index customers_lower_email_idx on customers (lower(email));
explain (analyze) select id from customers where lower(email) = 'user42@example.com';</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan (trimmed)</p><pre class="plain">Index Scan using customers_lower_email_idx on customers  (cost=0.28..8.29 rows=1 width=4) (actual rows=1 loops=1)
  Index Cond: (lower(email) = 'user42@example.com'::text)</pre><p class="codelabel">A type mismatch</p><pre>-- with an index on orders(customer_id) in place:
explain select * from orders where customer_id = 42.0;</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan</p><pre class="plain">Gather  (cost=1000.00..4356.71 rows=1000 width=29)
  Workers Planned: 1
  ->  Parallel Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..3256.71 rows=588 width=29)
        Filter: ((customer_id)::numeric = 42.0)</pre><p>The literal <code>42.0</code> is a <code>numeric</code>, so PostgreSQL cast the <strong>column</strong> to numeric for every row, which an index on the integer column cannot serve. The same happens with <code>customer_id::text = '42'</code>.</p><p class="codelabel">A leading wildcard</p><pre>explain (analyze) select id from customers where email like '%42@example.com';</pre><p class="codelabel">Plan (trimmed)</p><pre class="plain">Seq Scan on customers  (cost=0.00..42.00 rows=20 width=4) (actual rows=20 loops=1)
  Filter: (email ~~ '%42@example.com'::text)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 1980</pre><ul><li>A B-tree is sorted from the left, so it cannot find “ends with” or “contains”. For prefix matches such as <code>like 'user42%'</code>, the index needs <code>text_pattern_ops</code> in a database with a non-C collation: without it the lab used a Seq Scan, with it a <code>Bitmap Index Scan</code> with <code>Index Cond: ((email ~>=~ 'user42') AND (email ~<~ 'user43'))</code>.</li><li><strong>Low selectivity:</strong> on the lab’s <code>status</code> column, <code>status = 'paid'</code> (93% of rows) used a Seq Scan even with an index, while <code>status = 'refunded'</code> (2%) used the index. The planner compares costs; it is not being stubborn.</li></ul>`

</svg></div><p><code>EXPLAIN</code> shows the plan the database *would* use. <code>EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)</code> <strong>runs</strong> the query and adds what actually happened. Read it as a tree from the leaves up: each node passes its rows to its parent.</p><p class="codelabel">The index-only scan from earlier, annotated</p><pre class="plain">Index Only Scan using orders_cust_cover_idx on orders       <- scan type
  (cost=0.42..6.19 rows=101 width=8)                            <- estimate: 101 rows
  (actual time=0.083..0.104 rows=102 loops=1)                   <- reality: 102 rows
  Index Cond: (customer_id = 42)                                <- what the index used
  Heap Fetches: 0                                               <- table pages visited
  Buffers: shared hit=1 read=3                                  <- 1 page from cache, 3 from disk</pre><ul><li><strong>Estimated versus actual rows</strong> is the first thing to compare. 101 against 102 is healthy. A thousand-fold gap means stale or missing statistics, and the planner chose on bad information.</li><li><strong>Scan type:</strong> <code>Seq Scan</code> reads everything, <code>Bitmap Heap Scan</code> and <code>Index Scan</code> follow an index, <code>Index Only Scan</code> never visits the table.</li><li><strong><code>Rows Removed by Filter</code></strong> is wasted work: a large number on a small result says “you need an index”.</li><li><strong><code>Buffers</code></strong> counts pages. It is steadier than time, so use it to compare two plans.</li><li><strong><code>ANALYZE</code> executes the statement.</strong> Wrap an <code>UPDATE</code> or <code>DELETE</code> in <code>BEGIN</code> and <code>ROLLBACK</code>.</li></ul><p class="verified">Costs and times in the captured plans changed from run to run. Compare plan shapes and row counts.</p>`

      q:"Which index types exist beyond B-tree?",
      a:`<table class="cmp"><tr><th>Type</th><th>Good for</th><th>Example</th></tr><tr><td><strong>B-tree</strong> (default)</td><td>Equality, ranges, sorting, prefix <code>LIKE</code></td><td><code>created_at > ...</code>, <code>ORDER BY</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Hash</strong></td><td>Equality only; rarely better than a B-tree</td><td><code>session_token = ...</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>GIN</strong></td><td>Values that contain many keys: arrays, <code>jsonb</code>, full-text, trigrams</td><td><code>tags @> '{sql}'</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>GiST</strong></td><td>Ranges, geometry, nearest-neighbour</td><td>Overlapping time ranges, locations</td></tr><tr><td><strong>BRIN</strong></td><td>Huge tables whose values follow the physical order, at tiny size</td><td>An append-only log by timestamp</td></tr></table><p>The default is right far more often than not. Reach for another type when the data is not a scalar you compare: a <code>jsonb</code> document, an array, text you search, or a range.</p>`

    {
      q:"What do indexes cost on writes, and how many is too many?",
      a:`<p>Every index is another structure to update on each insert, on each update of an indexed column, and on delete. Reads get faster and writes get slower.</p><p class="codelabel">Measuring the write cost</p><pre>-- 100,000-row insert into orders, rolled back afterwards
explain (analyze, timing off) insert into orders (customer_id, status, total_cents, created_at)
select 1 + i % 1960, 'paid', 1000, now() from generate_series(1, 100000) i;</pre><p class="codelabel">Execution time, same statement</p><pre class="plain">with only the primary key and the foreign keys:   4172 ms
after adding three more indexes:                    5556 ms</pre><ul><li>Three extra indexes made this insert about a third slower in this run (timings vary, but the direction is stable).</li><li><strong>How many is too many:</strong> when writes slow measurably or the indexes together rival the table in size. Find the unused ones with <code>pg_stat_user_indexes</code> (<code>idx_scan = 0</code>) and drop them.</li><li><strong>Prefer fewer, wider composite indexes</strong> designed around your real queries over one index per column.</li><li><strong>Foreign keys:</strong> index the referencing column when you delete from the parent or join on it.</li></ul><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/performance-optimization" target="_top">Performance Optimisation</a></p>`
    },

      q:"Rapid-fire: indexing",

Not <code>b</code> alone.</td></tr><tr><td>What is an index-only scan?</td><td>The query is answered from the index; the table is not visited.</td></tr><tr><td>What is a partial index?</td><td>An index on only the rows matching a condition, which makes it small.</td></tr><tr><td>Why can <code>lower(col) = x</code> not use an index on <code>col</code>?</td><td>The index holds <code>col</code>, not <code>lower(col)</code>. Index the expression.</td></tr><tr><td>Which node in a plan shows wasted work?</td><td><code>Rows Removed by Filter</code>.</td></tr><tr><td>What do indexes cost?</td><td>Disk space and slower writes.</td></tr></table>`

      q:"What does ACID mean in practice?",
      a:`<table class="cmp"><tr><th>Letter</th><th>Promise</th><th>What it looks like</th></tr><tr><td><strong>Atomicity</strong></td><td>All of a transaction happens or none of it</td><td>A transfer debits and credits, or does neither</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Consistency</strong></td><td>Constraints hold before and after</td><td>A <code>CHECK (balance_cents >= 0)</code> rejects an overdraft</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Isolation</strong></td><td>Concurrent transactions do not see each other’s half-done work</td><td>Governed by the isolation level</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Durability</strong></td><td>Once committed, it survives a crash</td><td>Written to the write-ahead log (WAL) before <code>COMMIT</code> returns</td></tr></table><ul><li>Atomicity and durability are what people mean by “it is safe once the commit returns”.</li><li>Isolation is the subtle one: it is a <strong>dial</strong>, not a switch, and the next cards show what each setting allows.</li><li>Consistency here means the database’s own rules. Your business rules count only if you express them as constraints or enforce them in the transaction.</li></ul>`
    },
    {
      q:"Which anomalies can happen between concurrent transactions?",
      a:`<p>Each row below was reproduced with two real connections on PostgreSQL 17.6.</p><table class="cmp"><tr><th>Anomaly</th><th>READ COMMITTED (default)</th><th>REPEATABLE READ</th><th>SERIALIZABLE</th></tr><tr><td><strong>Dirty read</strong> (see uncommitted data)</td><td>Never</td><td>Never</td><td>Never</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Non-repeatable read</strong> (a row changes between two reads)</td><td>Happens</td><td>Prevented</td><td>Prevented</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Phantom</strong> (new rows appear between two reads)</td><td>Happens</td><td>Prevented in PostgreSQL</td><td>Prevented</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Lost update</strong> (read, then write a stale value)</td><td>Happens if you read then write</td><td>Prevented by an error</td><td>Prevented by an error</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Write skew</strong> (two writes break a shared rule)</td><td>Happens</td><td>Happens</td><td>Prevented by an error</td></tr></table><ul><li>PostgreSQL <strong>never allows a dirty read</strong>. Asking for <code>READ UNCOMMITTED</code> gives you <code>READ COMMITTED</code>: in the lab, a transaction set a balance to 0 without committing, and a second transaction at <code>READ UNCOMMITTED</code> still read 100.</li><li>The SQL standard allows phantoms at <code>REPEATABLE READ</code>; PostgreSQL’s snapshots do not. Do not assume another database matches.</li><li>“Prevented by an error” means the database aborts one transaction with SQLSTATE <code>40001</code> and <strong>you must retry it</strong>.</li></ul><p class="codelabel">Non-repeatable read and phantom, READ COMMITTED</p><pre class="plain">A read balance         100
B update to 70 (committed)
A read balance again   70            <- the row changed inside A's transaction

A count queued jobs    3
B insert a queued job (committed)
A count again          4             <- a new row appeared</pre><p class="codelabel">The same two tests at REPEATABLE READ</p><pre class="plain">A read balance 100, B updates to 70, A read again 100, after A commits: 70
A count 3, B inserts a job, A count again 3</pre>`

<text x="28" y="212"  font-family="var(--mono)" font-size="10.5" fill="var(--text)">Fix 1  do the arithmetic in the database, in one statement:</text><text x="28" y="230"  font-family="var(--mono)" font-size="10.5" fill="var(--accent)">UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = balance_cents - 30 WHERE id = 1</text>

FOR UPDATE, then write.</text></svg></div><p>The classic bug: the application reads a balance, computes a new value, and writes it back. Two requests interleave and one overwrites the other.</p><p class="codelabel">Captured with two connections, READ COMMITTED</p><pre class="plain">A begin, B begin

B read balance         100
A write 70             UPDATE 1
A commit
B write 50             UPDATE 1          <- B never saw A's change
B commit
final balance          50                <- should be 20: A's 30 is lost</pre><p><strong>Fix 1: let the database do the arithmetic.</strong> The second <code>UPDATE</code> waits for the first to commit, then re-reads the row and applies its change to the new value.</p><p class="codelabel">Same scenario with set balance_cents = balance_cents - 30 and - 50</p><pre class="plain">A update                UPDATE 1
B update                -- WAITING       <- blocked on A's row lock
A commit
B update                UPDATE 1         <- applied to 70, not to 100
B commit
final balance           20</pre><p><strong>Fix 2: lock the row when you read it</strong> with <code>SELECT ... FOR UPDATE</code>, when the new value needs logic in the application.</p><p class="codelabel">Captured</p><pre class="plain">A read for update        100
B read for update        -- WAITING
A write 70, A commit
B read for update        70               <- B now sees A's committed value
B write 20, B commit
final balance            20</pre><ul><li>A third fix is a version column and <code>UPDATE ... WHERE id = 1 AND version = 7</code>: <strong>optimistic locking</strong>, which retries when it updates zero rows.</li></ul>`

    {
      q:"What do READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE give you in PostgreSQL?",
      a:`<table class="cmp"><tr><th>Level</th><th>Each statement sees</th><th>Use it for</th><th>Cost</th></tr><tr><td><strong>READ COMMITTED</strong> (default)</td><td>Everything committed when that <strong>statement</strong> started</td><td>Most web requests</td><td>You must lock or write atomically to avoid lost updates</td></tr><tr><td><strong>REPEATABLE READ</strong></td><td>One snapshot, taken at the first statement</td><td>Reports and multi-query reads that must agree</td><td>Conflicting writes abort with a serialization error</td></tr><tr><td><strong>SERIALIZABLE</strong></td><td>A snapshot, plus conflict detection</td><td>Rules that span rows</td><td>More aborts; every transaction needs a retry</td></tr></table><p class="codelabel">A write that conflicts with a committed change, REPEATABLE READ (captured)</p><pre class="plain">A begin repeatable read
A read balance             100
B update balance to 70     (committed)
A update balance - 30      ERROR: could not serialize access due to concurrent update (SQLSTATE 40001)</pre><ul><li><strong>The rule:</strong> if you use <code>REPEATABLE READ</code> or <code>SERIALIZABLE</code>, wrap the transaction in a <strong>retry loop</strong> for SQLSTATE <code>40001</code> (and <code>40P01</code>, the deadlock). The cards on Node.js show one.</li><li>Most applications stay on <code>READ COMMITTED</code> and use <code>FOR UPDATE</code>, atomic <code>UPDATE</code> statements and unique constraints for the few places that need more.</li><li>Other databases name the same levels differently. MySQL’s InnoDB defaults to <code>REPEATABLE READ</code> and behaves differently in places.</li></ul>`

FOR UPDATE</code> locks the rows it returns, so other writers (and other <code>FOR UPDATE</code> readers) wait until you finish. <strong><code>SKIP LOCKED</code></strong> skips rows that are already locked, which is the standard way to build a job queue in a table.</p><p class="codelabel">Take the next free job</p><pre>select id from jobs where status = 'queued' order by id limit 1 for update skip locked;</pre><p class="codelabel">Two workers, captured</p><pre class="plain">A take a job   id 1
B take a job   id 2          <- B skipped the row A holds instead of waiting</pre><p>A <strong>deadlock</strong> happens when two transactions each hold a lock the other needs.</p><p class="codelabel">Captured</p><pre class="plain">A update row 1     UPDATE 1
B update row 2     UPDATE 1
A update row 2     -- WAITING
B update row 1     -- WAITING
A update row 2     ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)
                   DETAIL: Process 113 waits for ShareLock on transaction 880; blocked by process 114.

B update row 1     UPDATE 1                <- the survivor continues</pre><ul><li>PostgreSQL waits <code>deadlock_timeout</code> (1 second by default), finds the cycle and aborts one transaction. Which one is not something to rely on: in this run it was A.</li><li><strong>Prevent them</strong> by always locking rows in the same order (for example by id), keeping transactions short, and retrying on <code>40P01</code>.</li></ul>`

      q:"Quiz: Which isolation level prevents write skew in PostgreSQL? <span class=\"quizopts\">(A) READ COMMITTED  ·  (B) REPEATABLE READ  ·  (C) SERIALIZABLE  ·  (D) None: it needs application locks</span>",
      a:`<ol class="quiz" type="A"><li>READ COMMITTED</li><li>REPEATABLE READ</li><li class="right">SERIALIZABLE</li><li>None: it needs application locks</li></ol><p><strong>Answer: C.</strong> Only SERIALIZABLE. At REPEATABLE READ the lab let both transactions commit and left nobody on call. At SERIALIZABLE the second commit failed with SQLSTATE 40001 and had to be retried. Locking the rows is another valid fix, but the level itself that prevents it is SERIALIZABLE.</p>`

      q:"How do you approach a SQL question in an interview?",
      a:`<ol><li><strong>Restate it</strong> and ask about the edge cases: ties, NULLs, empty groups, duplicates.</li><li><strong>Name the grain</strong> of the result: one row per what? Per customer, per month, per department?</li><li><strong>Write the simplest correct query</strong> first, on a small example you can check by eye. Say the plan aloud: “join, group, then filter”.</li><li><strong>Check the traps:</strong> <code>NULL</code> in a <code>NOT IN</code>, a <code>LEFT JOIN</code> filtered in <code>WHERE</code>, <code>COUNT(*)</code> against <code>COUNT(col)</code>, integer division, time zones.</li><li><strong>Then talk about performance:</strong> which index would serve it, what the plan would do on a hundred million rows.</li></ol><p>Try any query against the practice tables.</p><div class="sqlrun" data-free="1"></div><p>Interviewers mostly watch for the first two steps. A correct query reached by clear steps beats a clever one-liner you cannot explain.</p><p><strong>Trap:</strong> Do not start typing at once. A candidate who asks “what if two people tie?” has already passed half the question.</p><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/coding-questions" target="_top">Coding Questions</a></p>`

    {
      q:"Puzzle: Find the second-highest salary",
      a:`<p>Return the second-highest <strong>distinct</strong> salary. Two people tie for the top salary.</p><p class="codelabel">Tables</p><pre class="plain">employees(id, name, department_id, manager_id, salary, hired_on)  -- 12 rows
Ada 150000, Grace 150000, Alan 120000, Linus 110000, Margaret 95000, Sam 90000,
Sue 85000, Sid 85000, Nora 72000, Cora 70000, Cal 65000, Fiona 60000</pre><div class="sqlrun" data-ordered="0"></div><details class="reveal"><summary>Show a solution</summary><p class="codelabel">SQL</p><pre>select name, salary from (
  select name, salary, dense_rank() over (order by salary desc) as r
  from employees) x
where r = 2;</pre><p class="codelabel">Result</p><pre class="plain">name | salary
-----+-------
Alan | 120000
(1 row)</pre><p><code>dense_rank</code> gives tied rows the same rank and does not skip numbers, so rank 2 is the second distinct salary. <code>rank</code> would skip to 3 after a tie.</p><p>The subquery form also works: <code>select max(salary) from employees where salary < (select max(salary) from employees)</code> returned <code>120000</code>.</p><p>The trap is <code>order by salary desc limit 1 offset 1</code>: with the tie at the top it returned <strong>Ada, 150000</strong>, the top salary again.</p></details>`
    },
    {
      q:"Puzzle: List the two highest-paid people in each department",
      a:`<p>One row per person, at most two per department. People with no department should be treated as their own group. If two people tie, any consistent choice is fine.</p><p class="codelabel">Tables</p><pre class="plain">employees(id, name, department_id, manager_id, salary, hired_on)  -- 12 rows
Ada 150000, Grace 150000, Alan 120000, Linus 110000, Margaret 95000, Sam 90000,
Sue 85000, Sid 85000, Nora 72000, Cora 70000, Cal 65000, Fiona 60000
Nora has no department.</pre><div class="sqlrun" data-ordered="0"></div><details class="reveal"><summary>Show a solution</summary><p class="codelabel">SQL</p><pre>select department_id, name, salary, rn from (
  select department_id, name, salary,
         row_number() over (partition by department_id order by salary desc, id) as rn
  from employees) x
where rn <= 2
order by department_id nulls last, rn;</pre><p class="codelabel">Result</p><pre class="plain">department_id | name  | salary | rn
--------------+-------+--------+---
            1 | Ada   | 150000 |  1
            1 | Grace | 150000 |  2
            2 | Sam   |  90000 |  1
            2 | Sue   |  85000 |  2
            3 | Cora  |  70000 |  1
            3 | Cal   |  65000 |  2
         NULL | Nora  |  72000 |  1
(7 rows)</pre><p><code>partition by</code> restarts the numbering for each department, and <code>NULL</code> values form a single partition, so Nora gets her own group.</p><p><code>row_number</code> always returns exactly two rows per department. With <code>rank</code> or <code>dense_rank</code> a tie at second place would return three. Choose by what the question means.</p><p>Without a tie-break in <code>order by</code> (here <code>id</code>), the choice between Ada and Grace is arbitrary and can change between runs.</p></details>`

      q:"How do you model one-to-many and many-to-many relationships?",
      a:`<p><strong>One-to-many:</strong> the “many” side holds a foreign key to the “one” side. <strong>Many-to-many:</strong> a <strong>join table</strong> holds a pair of foreign keys, with a composite primary key so a pair cannot repeat.</p><p class="codelabel">One author has many books; books and tags are many-to-many</p><pre>create table authors (id bigint generated always as identity primary key, name text not null);
create table books (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  author_id bigint not null references authors(id),
  title text not null
);
create index books_author_id_idx on books (author_id);   -- PostgreSQL does not index foreign keys for you

create table tags (id bigint generated always as identity primary key, name text not null unique);
create table book_tags (
  book_id bigint not null references books(id) on delete cascade,
  tag_id  bigint not null references tags(id),
  primary key (book_id, tag_id)
);</pre><p class="codelabel">Linking the same pair twice, captured</p><pre class="plain">insert into book_tags values (1, 1);   INSERT 1
insert into book_tags values (1, 1);
ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "book_tags_pkey"
DETAIL: Key (book_id, tag_id)=(1, 1) already exists.</pre><ul><li>The composite key does two jobs: it forbids duplicates and indexes lookups by <code>book_id</code>. Add a second index on <code>(tag_id, book_id)</code> for the reverse direction.</li><li>Index every foreign key that you join on or delete through. PostgreSQL indexes the referenced column (the primary key) but <strong>not</strong> the referencing one.</li><li><code>on delete cascade</code> removes dependent rows automatically. Use it for owned data (a book’s tag links) and not for data that should block the delete.</li><li>One-to-one is a one-to-many with a <code>unique</code> foreign key.</li></ul>`

      a:`<p>A PostgreSQL connection is a <strong>process</strong> that costs memory and a handshake to open. The server allows a fixed number of them.</p><p class="codelabel">Opening connections one after another, captured</p><pre class="plain">max_connections = 100

Session state (<code>SET</code>, advisory locks, prepared statements in some setups) does not survive, so keep each unit of work inside one transaction.</li><li>Set a pool <code>max</code>, a connection timeout and an idle timeout, and always release connections (<code>finally { client.release() }</code>).</li></ul><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/nodejs" target="_top">Node.js guide</a> · <a href="/aws" target="_top">AWS: RDS and RDS Proxy</a></p>`

      q:"How does SQL injection happen, and what actually prevents it?",
      a:`<p>It happens when user input is <strong>concatenated into the SQL text</strong>, so the input is parsed as SQL.       a:`<table class="cmp"><tr><th>Access pattern</th><th>Better fit</th><th>Example</th></tr><tr><td>Documents read and written whole, no joins</td><td><strong>Document store</strong> (MongoDB, DynamoDB used as documents)</td><td>A product catalogue, a user profile</td></tr><tr><td>Lookups by a single key at very high speed</td><td><strong>Key-value</strong> (Redis, DynamoDB)</td><td>Sessions, feature flags, counters</td></tr><tr><td>Huge write volume, time series, partitioned by key</td><td><strong>Wide-column</strong> (Cassandra, Bigtable)</td><td>Sensor readings, activity logs</td></tr><tr><td>Free-text relevance, facets, fuzzy matching</td><td><strong>Search engine</strong> (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch)</td><td>Product search</td></tr><tr><td>Queries that follow many hops of relationships</td><td><strong>Graph</strong> (Neo4j)</td><td>Recommendations, fraud rings</td></tr></table><p>PostgreSQL covers more of these than people expect (<code>jsonb</code>, full-text search, <code>LISTEN</code>, extensions), so the honest first question is whether you have <strong>outgrown</strong> it or just want something newer.</p><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/system-design" target="_top">System Design</a> · <a href="/aws" target="_top">AWS: DynamoDB</a></p>`

In a document store you model the <strong>queries</strong> and shape the data so one read returns what a screen needs.</p><table class="cmp"><tr><th></th><th>Embed</th><th>Reference</th></tr><tr><td><strong>Use when</strong></td><td>The child is read with the parent, is owned by it, and the list is bounded</td><td>The child is shared, grows without bound, or is read on its own</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Example</strong></td><td>An order and its line items</td><td>A product that appears in many orders</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Cost</strong></td><td>Duplicated data, and a large document if the list grows</td><td>A second read, and no join to help you</td></tr></table><ul><li>Embedding trades <strong>update cost for read speed</strong>: renaming a product means updating every order that embedded the name, or deciding that old orders should keep the name they were placed with (often the right business answer).</li><li>Without joins and cross-document transactions you carry consistency in the application, so list your access patterns before you design.</li></ul>`

      a:`<ul><li><strong>CAP:</strong> when the network <strong>partitions</strong>, a distributed store must choose between <strong>consistency</strong> (every read sees the latest write) and <strong>availability</strong> (every request gets an answer). It says nothing about the normal case, and “pick two of three” is a misleading summary: you do not get to opt out of partitions.</li><li><strong>PACELC</strong> adds the everyday trade-off: if there is a <strong>P</strong>artition, choose <strong>A</strong> or <strong>C</strong>; <strong>E</strong>lse (no partition), choose <strong>L</strong>atency or <strong>C</strong>onsistency. I would say that during a partition we must pick between consistency and availability, and that the more useful everyday question is latency against consistency.</div><p class="deeper"><strong>Go deeper:</strong> <a href="/system-design-scale" target="_top">System Design at Scale</a></p>`

window.addEventListener('message', (e)=>{
  if(!e.data) return;
  if(e.data.type==='goto-section') gotoQuestion(e.data.id, e.data.qIdx, false);
  else if(e.data.type==='start-weak-deck') startWeakDeck();
  else if(e.data.type==='start-deck') startKeyDeck(e.data.keys, e.data.title);
});
content.addEventListener('click', (e)=>{
  const a = e.target.closest('a[data-go]');
  if(a){ e.preventDefault(); const [id, q] = a.dataset.go.split(':'); gotoQuestion(id, Number(q), true); return; }
  const g = e.target.closest('button[data-goto]');
  if(g){ activeId = g.dataset.goto; hideBack(); renderNav(); renderContent(); window.scrollTo(0,0); return; }
  const act = e.target.closest('button[data-act]');
  if(act){
    if(act.dataset.act === 'listen'){ startListen(); return; }
    if(act.dataset.act === 'flash'){ startDeck(deckFromView(), searchTerm ? 'Search: ' + searchTerm : DATA.find(s=>s.id===activeId).title); return; }
    content.querySelectorAll('.qcard').forEach(c=> c.classList.toggle('open', act.dataset.act === 'expand'));
  }
});
content.addEventListener('change', (e)=>{
  const p = e.target.dataset && e.target.dataset.pref;
  if(!p) return;
  prefs[p] = e.target.checked; savePrefs();
  if(searchTerm) renderSearch(); else renderContent();
});

// ---- keyboard: / search, j/k move, o or Enter open, x reviewed, n/p section, Esc
let focusIdx = -1;
function cards(){ return Array.from(content.querySelectorAll('.qcard')); }
function setFocus(card, scroll){
  cards().forEach(c=> c.classList.remove('focused'));
  card.classList.add('focused');
  focusIdx = cards().indexOf(card);
  if(scroll) card.scrollIntoView({ block:'start', behavior:'smooth' });
}
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=>{
  if(fc.open){ fcKey(e); return; }
  if((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === 'k'){ e.preventDefault(); closeNav(); searchInput.focus(); searchInput.select(); return; }
  const typing = /INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT/.test(document.activeElement.tagName);
  if(e.key === 'Escape'){ if(searchTerm || searchInput.value){ clearSearch(); } searchInput.blur(); return; }
  if(typing || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey) return;
  const list = cards();
  if(e.key === '/'){ e.preventDefault(); searchInput.focus(); searchInput.select(); return; }
  if(e.key === 'j' || e.key === 'k'){
    if(!list.length) return;
    focusIdx = Math.max(0, Math.min(list.length - 1, focusIdx + (e.key === 'j' ? 1 : -1)));
    setFocus(list[focusIdx], true); return;
  }
  const cur = list[focusIdx];
  if((e.key === 'o' || e.key === 'Enter') && cur){ cur.classList.toggle('open'); return; }
  if(e.key === 'x' && cur){ setDone(cur, !reviewed[qKey(cur.dataset.sec, Number(cur.dataset.q))]); return; }
  if(e.key === 'n' || e.key === 'p'){
    if(searchTerm) return;
    const i = DATA.findIndex(s=>s.id===activeId) + (e.key === 'n' ? 1 : -1);
    if(DATA[i]){ activeId = DATA[i].id; hideBack(); renderNav(); renderContent(); window.scrollTo(0,0); }
  }
});


// ---- flashcards: question first, say the answer, reveal, rate yourself
const fcEl = document.getElementById('fc');
const fc = { open:false, deck:[], i:0, revealed:false, got:0, missed:[], again:new Map(), title:'', source:[] };
function shuffleArr(a){ for(let i=a.length-1;i>0;i--){ const j=Math.floor(Math.random()*(i+1)); const t=a[i]; a[i]=a[j]; a[j]=t; } return a; }
function startDeck(entries, title){
  stopListen();
  if(!entries.length) return;
  fc.source = entries.slice();
  fc.deck = prefs.shuffle ? shuffleArr(entries.slice()) : entries.slice();
  fc.i = 0; fc.revealed = false; fc.got = 0; fc.missed = []; fc.again = new Map(); fc.title = title; fc.open = true;
  fc.opener = document.activeElement;   // restore focus here when the dialog closes
  fcEl.querySelector('#fcShuffle').checked = !!prefs.shuffle;
  fcEl.hidden = false; document.body.classList.add('fc-lock');
  renderFc();
  fcEl.querySelector('.fc-dialog').focus();
}
function closeFc(){
  fc.open = false; fcEl.hidden = true; document.body.classList.remove('fc-lock');
  refreshWeakButton();
  const opener = fc.opener; fc.opener = null;
  if(searchTerm) renderSearch(); else renderContent();   // rebuilds #content, so `opener` may now be a detached node
  // Return focus to whatever opened the deck when it's still on the page (the hero "Flashcards"
  // buttons, outside #content, always survive this). Otherwise #content was just rebuilt under
  // the (now-detached) opener, so land on its heading instead of silently losing focus to <body>.
  if(opener && document.contains(opener)) opener.focus();
  else {
    const heading = content.querySelector('.section-head h2') || content.querySelector('.section-head');
    if(heading){ heading.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1'); heading.focus(); }
  }
}
function markReviewed(key, val){ reviewed[key] = val; writeJSON(STORAGE_KEY, reviewed); const p = key.split(':'); syncTitle(p[0], Number(p[1]), val); updateProgress(); renderNav(); }
function renderFc(){
  const n = fc.deck.length;
  fcEl.querySelector('.fc-title').textContent = fc.title;
  fcEl.querySelector('.fc-count').textContent = (fc.i < n ? (fc.i + 1) : n) + ' / ' + n + (fc.got ? ' · ' + fc.got + ' got it' : '') + (fc.missed.length ? ' · ' + new Set(fc.missed).size + ' to revisit' : '');
  fcEl.querySelector('.fc-bar i').style.width = (n ? fc.i / n * 100 : 0) + '%';
  const body = fcEl.querySelector('.fc-body');
  const actions = fcEl.querySelector('.fc-actions');
  if(fc.i >= n){
    const uniqMissed = Array.from(new Set(fc.missed));
    body.innerHTML = '<div class="fc-done"><h3>Deck finished</h3><p>' + fc.got + ' marked "got it" (and ticked as reviewed) · ' + uniqMissed.length + ' to revisit.</p>' +
      (uniqMissed.length ? '<p class="fc-sub">To revisit:</p><ul>' + uniqMissed.map(e=>'<li>' + e.item.q + '</li>').join('') + '</ul>' : '<p class="fc-sub">Nothing missed. Well done.</p>') + '</div>';
    actions.innerHTML = (uniqMissed.length ? '<button data-fc="missed" class="primary">Practise the ' + uniqMissed.length + ' missed</button>' : '') +
      '<button data-fc="restart">Restart deck</button><button data-fc="close">Close <kbd>Esc</kbd></button>';
    return;
  }
  const e = fc.deck[fc.i];
  const key = qKey(e.section.id, e.qIdx);
  body.innerHTML = '<div class="qchips"><span class="qsec">' + e.section.title + '</span>' + (CORE.has(key) ? '<span class="qcore">★ core</span>' : '') + (reviewed[key] ? '<span class="qsec">reviewed</span>' : '') + '</div>' +
    '<h3 class="fc-q">' + e.item.q + '</h3>' +
    (fc.revealed ? '<div class="qbody fc-a">' + e.item.a + '</div>' : '<p class="fc-prompt">Answer it out loud first: the main point, one example, one trade-off. Then reveal.</p>');
  enhance(body);
  body.scrollTop = 0;
  actions.innerHTML = fc.revealed
    ? '<button data-fc="prev" title="Previous (←)">←</button><button data-fc="again" class="again">Again <kbd>1</kbd></button><button data-fc="got" class="primary">Got it <kbd>2</kbd></button>'
    : '<button data-fc="prev" title="Previous (←)">←</button><button data-fc="reveal" class="primary">Reveal answer <kbd>Space</kbd></button><button data-fc="skip">Skip <kbd>→</kbd></button>';
}
function fcAction(act){
  const n = fc.deck.length, e = fc.deck[fc.i];
  if(act === 'close') return closeFc();
  if(act === 'restart') return startDeck(fc.source, fc.title);
  if(act === 'missed') return startDeck(Array.from(new Set(fc.missed)), fc.title + ' · missed');
  if(fc.i >= n && act !== 'prev') return;
  if(act === 'reveal'){ fc.revealed = !fc.revealed; }
  else if(act === 'got'){ if(!fc.revealed){ fc.revealed = true; } else { markReviewed(qKey(e.section.id, e.qIdx), true); markWeak(e.tkey, false); fc.got++; fc.i++; fc.revealed = false; } }
  else if(act === 'again'){
    if(!fc.revealed){ fc.revealed = true; }
    else {
      const k = qKey(e.section.id, e.qIdx), times = fc.again.get(k) || 0;
      fc.missed.push(e);
      markWeak(e.tkey, true);
      if(times < 2){ fc.deck.push(e); fc.again.set(k, times + 1); }   // comes back later in this session
      fc.i++; fc.revealed = false;
    }
  }
  else if(act === 'skip'){ fc.i++; fc.revealed = false; }
  else if(act === 'prev'){ if(fc.i > 0){ fc.i--; fc.revealed = false; } }
  renderFc();
}
fcEl.addEventListener('click', (e)=>{
  if(e.target === fcEl) return closeFc();
  const b = e.target.closest('button[data-fc]');
  if(b) return fcAction(b.dataset.fc);
  const a = e.target.closest('a[data-go]');
  if(a){ e.preventDefault(); closeFc(); const p = a.dataset.go.split(':'); gotoQuestion(p[0], Number(p[1]), true); }
});
fcEl.querySelector('#fcShuffle').addEventListener('change', (e)=>{
  prefs.shuffle = e.target.checked; savePrefs();
  const keep = fc.i + (fc.revealed ? 1 : 0);
  const rest = fc.deck.slice(keep);
  if(prefs.shuffle) shuffleArr(rest);
  fc.deck = fc.deck.slice(0, keep).concat(rest);
  renderFc();
});
function fcFocusables(){
  return Array.from(fcEl.querySelectorAll('button, input, a[href], [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])')).filter((el) => !el.disabled && el.offsetParent !== null);
}
function fcKey(e){
  if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); closeFc(); return; }
  if(e.key === 'Tab'){
    // trap focus inside the dialog: wrap from the last focusable back to the first, and vice versa
    const items = fcFocusables();
    if(!items.length) return;
    const idx = items.indexOf(document.activeElement);
    const next = e.shiftKey ? (idx <= 0 ? items.length - 1 : idx - 1) : (idx === items.length - 1 ? 0 : idx + 1);
    e.preventDefault();
    items[next].focus();
    return;
  }
  if(e.target && e.target.id === 'fcShuffle') return;
  const map = { ' ':'reveal', 'Enter':'reveal', '1':'again', '2':'got', 'ArrowRight':'skip', 'ArrowLeft':'prev' };
  const act = map[e.key];
  if(!act) return;
  if(e.target && e.target.tagName === 'BUTTON' && (e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'Enter')) return;   // let a focused button click itself
  e.preventDefault();
  if(fc.i >= fc.deck.length && act !== 'prev') return;
  fcAction(act);
}
function deckFromView(){ return cards().map(c=> entry(c.dataset.sec, Number(c.dataset.q))); }
document.getElementById('fcCore').addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(CORE.size) startDeck(Array.from(CORE).map(k=>{ const p = k.split(':'); return entry(p[0], Number(p[1])); }).filter(Boolean), 'All ★ core questions');
  else startDeck(INDEX.filter(e=>e.section.id!=='quickref'), 'All questions');
});

// ---- weak cards: any card marked "Again" (anywhere, including another guide), still unresolved
const fcWeakBtn = document.getElementById('fcWeak');
function weakOnThisGuide(){ return INDEX.filter(e=> weak[e.tkey]); }
function refreshWeakButton(){
  if(!fcWeakBtn) return;
  const n = weakOnThisGuide().length;
  fcWeakBtn.hidden = n === 0;
  fcWeakBtn.textContent = '↻ Review ' + n + ' weak card' + (n===1?'':'s');
}
function startWeakDeck(){
  if(fc.open) return;   // the #weak deep link retries its message for a few seconds; ignore repeats once the deck is open, or every retry would reset the user's progress in it
  const list = weakOnThisGuide();
  if(list.length) startDeck(list, 'Weak cards');
}
if(fcWeakBtn) fcWeakBtn.addEventListener('click', startWeakDeck);
// A deck named by card keys ("sec:idx"), opened from a link such as /sql#deck=sq1:0,sq1:1. The link's
// message is posted repeatedly for a few seconds, so ignore it once a deck is open; unknown keys are dropped.
function startKeyDeck(keys, title){
  if(fc.open || !Array.isArray(keys)) return;
  const list = keys.map(k=>{ const p = String(k).split(':'); return entry(p[0], Number(p[1])); }).filter(Boolean);
  if(list.length) startDeck(list, title || 'Your deck');
}
refreshWeakButton();
window.addEventListener('storage', (e)=>{ if(e.key === WEAK_KEY){ weak = readJSON(WEAK_KEY, {}); refreshWeakButton(); } });

document.getElementById('resetBtn').addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!confirm('Clear all reviewed checkmarks?')) return;
  reviewed = {}; writeJSON(STORAGE_KEY, reviewed);
  INDEX.forEach(e=>{ delete titleDone[e.tkey]; }); writeJSON(TITLES_KEY, titleDone);
  renderNav(); renderContent(); updateProgress();
});

document.getElementById('heroMeta').textContent = DATA.length + ' sections · ' + totalQuestions() + ' questions' + (CORE.size ? ' · ' + CORE.size + ' marked ★ core (linked from ' + window.__STUDY__.core + ')' : '');
document.getElementById('fcCore').textContent = CORE.size ? '▶ Flashcards: all ★ core questions' : '▶ Flashcards: all ' + INDEX.filter(e=>e.section.id!=='quickref').length + ' questions';
// ---- solo:start
// /study/<guide>.html?card=sec:idx shows just that one card, so a page elsewhere on the site (a mock
// round, a plan) can embed a card in an iframe. The frame is told how tall the card is.
function soloKey(search){ const m = /[?&]card=([^&#]+)/.exec(search || ''); return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null; }
function soloRender(key){
  document.documentElement.classList.add('solo');
  content.innerHTML = '';
  const p = key.split(':');
  const e = entry(p[0], Number(p[1]));
  if(!e){ const m = document.createElement('p'); m.className = 'empty'; m.textContent = 'This card has moved.'; content.appendChild(m); }
  else content.appendChild(buildCard(e, { open: true }));
  const post = ()=>{ try{ parent.postMessage({ type:'solo-height', card:key, height: Math.ceil(content.getBoundingClientRect().height) }, '*'); }catch(_){} };
  if(window.ResizeObserver) new ResizeObserver(post).observe(content);
  post();
}
// ---- solo:end
initListen();
const SOLO = soloKey(location.search);
if(SOLO){ soloRender(SOLO); updateProgress(); }
else { renderNav(); renderContent(); updateProgress(); }
